newsitem.title: BULGARIA: Bulgaria needs fresh loans to repay debt - Finmin.
newsitem.headline: Bulgaria needs fresh loans to repay debt - Finmin.

text.p: Bulgaria must rely entirely on external loans to repay foreign debt of nearly one billion dollars due this year, Finance Minister Svetoslav Gavriisky said on Thursday.

"Without financial support from the European Union and international lending institutions we will not be able to service our obligations to these organisations due this year," Gavriisky told reporters.

Speaking after the first session of the new interim cabinet, he said that some $200 million due to the EU and $126 million to the Paris Club of official creditors could be repaid only by new EU loans.
"We hope to receive between $300 million and $400 million from the EU," said Gavriisky.

Missions are expected in the next few days from the European Union, and from the International Monetary Fund, which suspended credits last year because of the ruling Socialists' failure to carry out promised reforms.

Coupon payments on Brady bonds issued two years ago to restructure an $8.16 billion commercial debt due in July should not be a problem if Bulgaria received funding for its other debts, said Gavriisky.

The cabinet, led by Sofia mayor Stefan Sofianski, has inherited economic chaos from the outgoing Socialist administration. Bulgaria has been without effective government since Zhan Videnov resigned as premier and party leader on December 21.

The cabinet also set up a Financial Stabilisation Council headed by Sofianski and including Gavriisky, central bank governor Lyubomir Filipov, Chavdar Kanchev, director of Bulgarian foreign trade bank Bulbank, and former debt negotiator Ventsislav Antonov.
The council will implement a financial stabilisation policy and negotiate with international lenders. -- Elisaveta Konstantinova, Sofia Newsroom, 359-2-84561
